items.title: Pentagon Inspector General Details U.S. Losses and Challenges in Iran War
items.author: John Ismay
items.content: <article>Helicopters for evacuating casualties were pulled from four countries, and hundreds of military facilities were destroyed, according to a new report.</article>

items.title: Trump Approves $2.8 Billion Arms Sale to Israel, Including 40,000 One-Ton Bombs
items.author: Michael Crowley and Edward Wong
items.content: <article>The package would be among the largest deliveries of U.S. munitions to Israel.</article>

items.title: Trump Plans Blitz of $138 Million and Counting to Save Midterm Republicans
items.author: Theodore Schleifer, Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
items.content: <article>His powerful super PAC is suddenly spending heavily on some races, after drawing fire from some Republicans that the group might not throw its weight behind the party’s candidates.</article>

items.title: Federal Employees Were Paid $9.5 Billion Not to Work in 2025 Under DOGE Effort
items.author: Eileen Sullivan
items.content: <article>As part of the Department of Government Efficiency’s program to shrink the federal work force, paid administrative leave costs rose by 435 percent.</article>

items.title: Melania Trump Encourages Children to Build ‘the Next Great Robot’ With A.I.
items.author: Erica L. Green
items.content: <article>The first lady, who has been a champion of A.I. during her husband’s second term, said the Mountain View Elementary School students should be at the forefront of technology.</article>

items.title: Trump Defended A.I. Data Centers on Truth Social, and Commenters Clapped Back
items.author: Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>The president’s posts about artificial intelligence on the social media platform he founded were met with an unusual volume of criticism.</article>

items.title: McCarthy Gets a Portrait Marking His Brief, Strange Speakership
items.author: Annie Karni
items.content: <article>Kevin McCarthy, the first speaker to be ousted from the post, was honored at the Capitol at the unveiling of his official portrait.</article>

items.title: House Kills Bid to Impeach Trump as Democrats Split
items.author: Michael Gold
items.content: <article>Dozens of Democrats declined to register a position on articles of impeachment by one of their own members, Representative Al Green, that cited President Trump’s immigration crackdown.</article>

items.title: ‘60 Minutes’ Season Premiere Sees Dip in Ratings
items.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
items.content: <article>Just under 8 million people watched Sunday’s season premiere, down 21 percent from last year. Viewership for the N.F.L. lead-in fell by about the same.</article>

items.title: Independent Budget Office Estimates Iran War Has Cost $38 Billion
items.author: Catie Edmondson
items.content: <article>The Congressional Budget Office said its analysis had been limited by the fact that the Defense Department did not respond to requests for information on the costs of the conflict.</article>

items.title: Kash Patel Suggests FBI Agents Could Go to Election Polling Sites
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>Federal law prohibits armed federal officers or military personnel from being deployed to polling stations.</article>

items.title: Here’s the latest.
items.author: Alan Feuer

items.title: Half of Voters Dislike Socialism Amid Progressive Wins, New Poll Finds
items.author: Kellen Browning and Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor and democratic socialist, was viewed more favorably than Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a fellow high-profile member of the movement.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Stands Up to Trump on Mail Voting and a Few Key Issues
items.author: Adam Liptak
items.content: <article>The justices take their time and pick their spots, but they have rejected presidential initiatives on tariffs, citizenship, the National Guard — and now the coming election.</article>

items.title: A.I. Is Unpopular With Voters, a New York Times/Siena Poll Finds
items.author: Tim Balk and Caroline Soler
items.content: <article>As fears grow about the threat of artificial intelligence, neither party has claimed an advantage on the technology, a New York Times/Siena poll found. But voters are united in opposition to data centers.</article>

items.title: How the Postal Service Became Central to U.S. Elections
items.author: Dan Watson
items.content: <article>The mail system took on new prominence during the Civil War by enabling soldiers to vote from afar. On Monday, the Supreme Court blocked President Trump’s effort to give it a new role in elections.</article>

items.title: Congress Has Proposed Many Bills for A.I. Regulation. Lawmakers Have Enacted Few.
items.author: Tony Romm, Dustin Volz and Michael Gold
items.content: <article>For years, Democrats and Republicans have proposed bills to address the greatest threats posed by artificial intelligence. Many remain stymied by political disputes.</article>

items.title: FEMA Could Still Lose More Jobs Despite Court Ruling
items.author: Scott Dance
items.content: <article>A plan to halve the agency’s sprawling work force was illegal, a judge ruled. But the court is not blocking other FEMA cuts.</article>

items.title: Trump Slams Supreme Court Over Mail-In Voting Ruling
items.author: Tyler Pager
items.content: <article>In a blistering attack on the court, President Trump said “these are not the people I interviewed” to serve as justices.</article>

items.title: A ‘Blue Wave’ May Be Building, but How High?
items.author: Nate Cohn
items.content: <article>A Times/Siena national poll suggests Republicans are reeling. Can they come back by depicting Democrats as too far to the left?</article>

items.title: U.S. Has Deployed Weapons in Space, Air Force Secretary Says
items.author: Francesca Regalado
items.content: <article>Troy E. Meink’s comments were the first public acknowledgment of American weapons in orbit. The Pentagon has been preparing for potential conflict in space with Russia or China.</article>

items.title: With Trump’s Plans Blocked, States Work to Restore Trust in Mail Voting
items.author: Nick Corasaniti, Anna Griffin and Richard Fausset
items.content: <article>President Trump’s efforts to restrict mail voting ahead of the midterms were thwarted by the Supreme Court, but they have sowed confusion and doubt among some voters.</article>

items.title: Democrats Gain Midterms Edge as Trump Drags Down Republicans, Per Times/Siena Poll
items.author: Shane Goldmacher, Ruth Igielnik and Sophia June
items.content: <article>Even some Republicans are losing faith in Trump’s economy, a New York Times/Siena poll found, and Democrats were favored on the top issues as the sprint to the midterms gets underway.</article>
